_why: §3j.154 — the game facts CI cannot re-derive, pinned so a change to one is deliberate and reviewable. Found by scripts/mutation-sweep.mjs --ci, which corrupts a real artefact and reports what still ships green. Two facts survived the CI gate: a reworded item description, and a wrong `dlc`. Both are things the site asserts about the game.
_layers: LOCAL proves these against the game itself (data:diff compares descriptions verbatim, data:verify checks dlc against ItemDef). CI has no game data — .decompiled/ and .gamedata/ are Gearbox's and never committed — so CI proves only that nothing changed since that proof. Neither layer alone is enough; together they are.
_notScopedHere: tier is deliberately absent: a wrong tier already fails the browser suite in CI, and guarding what is covered is upkeep for no cover (audit rule 7).

_descStatus.verbatim: matches the game's own _DESC token, which is what schema.ts documents
_descStatus.documented-divergence: differs deliberately, via descriptionNote + code/asset confidence
_descStatus.undocumented-divergence: differs with NO stated reason — see AUDIT-BACKLOG DEFERRED
_descStatus.no-game-text: quest/scrap items with no _DESC token, and the seven elite aspects whose _DESC is literally "???" — the game states nothing to quote (§3j.160)

_gameTags: §3j.166 — mechanical ItemDef tags, pinned from the game's own defs so a patch that changes an item's obtainability or immunity surfaces instead of passing silently. NOT published on the site yet: doing that needs a schema field and a UI surface, which is a DEFERRED decision. Display tags (Damage, Utility, Healing…) are excluded — they are the game's search vocabulary and assert nothing.
_fieldClaims: §3j.169/§3j.170 — every `fieldName <number>` pair our prose attaches to one of the game's own serialized fields, across descriptionNotes AND stacking formulas. LOCALLY, data:audit checks each against the extracted component/state data and the decompiled C#, against the SPECIFIC component a note names, and against the C# field INITIALISER — the last of which is how Frost Relic was caught publishing 22m/+6m from `icicleBaseRadius = 10f` when its own prefab serializes 6, "correcting" a game description that was right. CI has none of those extractions, so this pins the claims instead: the same parser (src/lib/fieldClaims.ts) re-derives them and they must match exactly. §3j.169 pinned only notes, and both formula mutations then survived --ci; formulas are included now. LIMIT, stated rather than hidden: a claim on a field name absent from `vocabulary` is invisible to CI and caught only locally, because CI cannot know the name is a game field at all.
